guidelines: Regular lecture attendance (minimum 75% required for exam eligibility)
Complete all continuous assessments (CAs) and assignments
Participate in tutorials and practical sessions
Form or join study groups for difficult courses
Obtain and review course outlines and past questions
Create revision timetable covering all courses
Focus on topics emphasized by lecturers
Practice with past exam papers under timed conditions
Review key formulas, definitions, and concepts
Clarify difficult topics with lecturers or peers
Ensure all required textbooks/materials are available

examination_registration_requirements: Payment of all school fees and charges
Registration within university portal before deadline

before_entering_exam_hall: Arrive at least 30 minutes before exam start time
Carry only permitted materials in transparent bag
Switch off mobile phone and leave with invigilators or outside
prohibited_items: Books, notes, or paper (unless open-book exam)
Food (unless for medical reasons with prior approval)

in_examination_hall_protocol: Sit only at assigned seat number
Fill answer booklet cover correctly (matric number, course code)
Read through entire question paper before starting
Allocate time according to marks distribution
Write legibly and use official answer booklet only
Raise hand quietly for any assistance needed
Do not communicate with other candidates
Do not leave hall within first 30 minutes or last 15 minutes

examination_conduct_rules.rule: Silence must be observed at all times
No borrowing of materials during exam
All work must be done during allotted time
Answer booklets must not contain identifying marks
Remain seated until all scripts are collected

types_of_examinations.description: For science, engineering, medical and vocational courses
Common for language courses and final projects

special_examination_circumstances.procedure: Inform invigilator immediately, obtain medical report, apply for special consideration
Submit formal application with evidence (medical report, police report) within 48 hours
Report to exams office immediately upon seeing timetable
Register with Student Affairs for accommodations (extra time, scribe, separate room)

post_examination_processes.description: Lecturers mark scripts anonymously (matric numbers only)
External examiners review marking and standards
Final approval of all examination results
Posted on notice boards and/or student portals

result_related_processes.description: Students can view results online or on departmental notice boards
Formal application for script viewing within 2 weeks of result publication
Failed courses must be registered again in following session
Some universities offer second chance exams for borderline failures

nuc_examination_standards: Minimum of 70% pass mark for professional courses
External examiner system mandatory for all programs
Examination malpractices must be reported to NUC
Results must be approved by Senate

grade_point_computation_nigeria.grading_system: Based on the National Universities Commission (NUC) standards

steps: 1. For each course, multiply the grade point by the course credit load (units)
2. Sum all quality points (Grade Point × Credit Units) for all courses
4. Divide total quality points by total credit units
cgpa_calculation.formula: CGPA = Σ(Grade Point × Credit Units) / Σ(Credit Units)

special_cases.description: Failed courses must be retaken; new grade replaces old grade in some universities
Given when student hasn't completed course requirements
Students with GPA below 1.5 (varies) may be placed on academic probation

university_misconduct_nigeria.governing_body: National Universities Commission (NUC) - Sets minimum standards, but individual universities establish specific codes of conduct

examples: Bringing unauthorized materials into exam hall
Leaking or obtaining exam questions before exam
penalties: Criminal prosecution under Examination Malpractice Act (1999)

examples: Submitting same work for multiple courses
penalties: Withdrawal of awarded degree if discovered later
Permanent exclusion from all Nigerian universities

disciplinary_procedures.description: Departmental or Security Committee investigates allegations
Student given opportunity to defend themselves
Committee submits recommendations to Senate or Governing Council
Final decision made by Senate/Governing Council
Students can usually appeal within specified time frame

nuc_regulations.description: NUC requires all universities to have published codes of conduct
Federal law prescribing penalties for exam malpractice

grading_impact_of_misconduct.impact: Failure in project/thesis, affecting final class of degree
All courses for that semester recorded as 'F' (0.0)
Permanent record of misconduct; no degree awarded

notes: 1. NUC provides framework but individual universities have specific codes of conduct
2. Penalties may vary between federal, state, and private universities
3. Some universities use 4-point scale instead of 5-point (check specific institution)
4. Students' Union activities are regulated under separate guidelines
5. All universities must have Students' Disciplinary Committees as per NUC requirements
6. Special disciplinary committees exist for staff misconduct
7. Examination timetables are usually released 2-3 weeks before exams
8. Continuous assessment typically constitutes 30-40% of final grade
9. Examination malpractice cases are handled by Special Examination Misconduct Committees
